finding.claim: SQL injection via unsanitized ORDER BY parameter in list_users_sorted(). The GET 'sort' value is concatenated directly into the query. An attacker can inject subqueries or CASE expressions for blind data extraction from any table in the SQLite DB (e.g. sort=(CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(password,1,1) FROM users LIMIT 1)='a' THEN id ELSE name END)). Stacked queries are not generally possible via PDO sqlite query(), but boolean/error-based blind extraction is.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) (list.php:6)

trace.note: string concatenation into ORDER BY clause, executed with PDO::query (not parameterizable, no allowlist)

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, no escaping, no authentication/authorization check in the file. Contrast with list_users_safe() (line 10-11), which uses an allowlist map, and find_user() (line 16), which uses a prepared statement; neither protects this function. Only these two other functions in the codebase were reviewed; no callers exist in the repo, so reachability depends on the function being invoked by a web entrypoint, but it reads $_GET directly so it is assumed web-reachable.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 takes $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it into an ORDER BY clause with no allowlist or escaping, and the allowlist at list.php:10-11 is only in list_users_safe(), so it does not protect this function.

verdict_facts.reason: list.php:5-6 passes $_GET['sort'] unvalidated into the ORDER BY of a PDO query(), with no allowlist, escaping, or auth check. The allowlist at list.php:10-11 is only in list_users_safe(), a different function.
